content.content:
1	# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)
2	
3	`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
4	macOS/Windows — CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb
5	(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` uses `xvfb-run` on `ubuntu-latest`), which is what this reproduces
6	locally, so a run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host.
7	
8	## Invoke
9	
10	```bash
11	npm run test:e2e:docker                    # whole suite, desktop
12	npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke   # one CI-style group
13	npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile             # mobile-emulation config
14	```
15	
16	Both wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose` (`docker-compose.yml` in this
17	directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also validates `--group` against
18	`scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir handling described below.
19	
20	The image builds automatically on first run (and on any later `Dockerfile`/`package.json`
21	change, via Docker's own layer cache) — pass `--build` to force a rebuild.
22	
23	## What's actually verified, not assumed
24	
25	Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
26	app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
27	it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
28	uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
29	one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.
30	
31	## Design choices
32	
33	**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
34	default, or one group with `--group`. Never one container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`
35	inside the container already dispatches every spec in scope through a single wdio run,
36	parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers, so batching multiple files per container
37	invocation is inherited from the existing script rather than reimplemented here. This
38	deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
39	matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
40	testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.
41	
42	`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
43	CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
44	Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
45	`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
46	give.
47	
48	**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
49	`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime, `docker-compose.yml`
50	mounts a *named volume* over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the bind-mounted repo's
51	`node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules` (wrong-platform native binaries)
52	would sit in front of the image's. Docker seeds a fresh named volume from the image's content at
53	that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra setup step. A second named volume
54	persists `.obsidian-cache` (the downloaded Obsidian build, ~150-250MB) across runs.
55	
56	**Rebuild the image or drop the `e2e-node-modules` volume** after a dependency change that isn't
57	reflected in a rebuild for some reason: `docker volume rm docker_e2e-node-modules` (the exact
58	name is prefixed by whatever `docker compose` derives from this directory — `docker volume ls`
59	to check).
60	
61	## Worktree caveat
62	
63	A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
64	(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
65	that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
66	`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
67	a git repository".
68	
69	`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
70	arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
71	bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
72	more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and

# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)

`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
macOS/Windows — CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` uses `xvfb-run` on `ubuntu-latest`), which is what this reproduces
locally, so a run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host.

## Invoke

```bash
npm run test:e2e:docker                    # whole suite, desktop
npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke   # one CI-style group
npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile             # mobile-emulation config
```

Both wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose` (`docker-compose.yml` in this
directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also validates `--group` against
`scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir handling described below.

The image builds automatically on first run (and on any later `Dockerfile`/`package.json`
change, via Docker's own layer cache) — pass `--build` to force a rebuild.

## What's actually verified, not assumed

Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Design choices

**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
default, or one group with `--group`. Never one container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`
inside the container already dispatches every spec in scope through a single wdio run,
parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers, so batching multiple files per container
invocation is inherited from the existing script rather than reimplemented here. This
deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.

`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
give.

**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime, `docker-compose.yml`
mounts a *named volume* over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the bind-mounted repo's
`node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules` (wrong-platform native binaries)
would sit in front of the image's. Docker seeds a fresh named volume from the image's content at
that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra setup step. A second named volume
persists `.obsidian-cache` (the downloaded Obsidian build, ~150-250MB) across runs.

**Rebuild the image or drop the `e2e-node-modules` volume** after a dependency change that isn't
reflected in a rebuild for some reason: `docker volume rm docker_e2e-node-modules` (the exact
name is prefixed by whatever `docker compose` derives from this directory — `docker volume ls`
to check).

## Worktree caveat

A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
a git repository".

`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and
target path are identical, confirmed with a plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before
reaching for the env-var approach instead.) A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this —
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already `.git` under the mounted root.

obvious choice, wrapping the whole invocation in `xvfb-run --auto-servernum`, hung indefinitely in
this container: `Xvfb` came up but the wrapped `node` process never started, because the
`wait`/`SIGUSR1` handshake `xvfb-run`'s own shell script uses for readiness never completed.

volume from what's already visible at that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra
setup step.

installer, and the Electron/Chromedriver build — ~490MB together, measured) across container
runs — scoped to exactly those subdirectories under `.obsidian-cache`, deliberately NOT the whole
directory: `e2e-summary.json` and `e2e-reports/` (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section) land
under `.obsidian-cache` too, on every run, and need to stay on the bind-mounted host filesystem —
`cat .obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` right after the container exits is the whole point of that
file. An earlier version of this compose file shadowed the whole directory with one volume, which
worked but made the summary invisible outside the container; this is why it doesn't.

**Rebuild the image or drop a volume** after a dependency or Obsidian-version change that isn't
reflected some other way: `docker volume ls` to see the actual names (`docker compose` prefixes
them, e.g. `docker_e2e-node-modules`), `docker volume rm <name>` to drop one.

**Rebuild the image or drop a volume** after a dependency or Obsidian-version change that isn't
reflected some other way: `docker volume ls` to see the actual names (`docker compose` prefixes
them, e.g. `docker_e2e-node-modules`), `docker volume rm <name>` to drop one.

## Worktree caveat

A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
a git repository".

`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and
target path are identical, confirmed with a plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before
reaching for the env-var approach instead.) A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this —
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already `.git` under the mounted root.

1	/**
2	 * Runs the e2e suite inside a Linux container under Xvfb — see
3	 * `e2e/docker/README.md` for what this buys over running locally (nothing
4	 * pops up on the host, whatever OS the host is) and its limits.
5	 *
6	 *   node scripts/e2e-docker.mjs [desktop|mobile] [--group <name>] [--build]
7	 *
8	 * One container per invocation, however many spec files that covers — every
9	 * spec (the default) or one CI-style group with `--group`. Not one
10	 * container per spec file: `docker compose run` already dispatches to
11	 * `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`, which runs every spec in scope through a single
12	 * wdio invocation, parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers inside
13	 * that one container — so batching is inherited, not reimplemented here.
14	 *
15	 * This deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run groups in
16	 * parallel, the way CI's matrix does: CI already gives full-suite,
17	 * parallel-across-groups coverage (see CLAUDE.md's "E2E testing" section —
18	 * it's the source of truth for that), so this script's job is narrower:
19	 * let a local run happen without a window, not out-race the matrix.
20	 *
21	 * `--build` forces a rebuild even if Docker thinks the image is current
22	 * (e.g. after bumping the Node base image) — ordinarily `docker compose run`
23	 * already rebuilds on a Dockerfile/package.json change via its own layer
24	 * cache, so this is rarely needed.
25	 */
26	
27	import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
28	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
29	import * as path from 'node:path';
30	import { specGroups } from './spec-groups.mjs';
31	
32	const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
33	const composeFile = path.join(root, 'e2e', 'docker', 'docker-compose.yml');
34	
35	/**
36	 * A git WORKTREE's `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
37	 * (`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree
38	 * alone gives the container that pointer with nothing at the far end, so
39	 * every git-invoking step (the build stamp in esbuild.config.mjs, and
40	 * `git status`/`checkout` in scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs) fails with "not
41	 * a git repository".
42	 *
43	 * Bind-mounting the real git dir at the SAME absolute path — the more
44	 * obvious fix — does not work here: this host (OrbStack) silently fails a
45	 * bind mount whose source and target path are identical, confirmed with a
46	 * plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before reaching for this. So
47	 * instead the git dir is mounted at an arbitrary container path and
48	 * `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` point git at it directly,
49	 * bypassing `.git`-file resolution entirely — verified against `git status`
50	 * and `git rev-parse` inside the container, not just rev-parse alone, since
51	 * check-vault-drift.mjs needs the former.
52	 *
53	 * A plain (non-worktree) checkout's `--git-common-dir` is just `.git` under
54	 * the already-mounted root, so this is a no-op there.
55	 */
56	function gitVolumeAndEnvArgs() {
57	  const commonDir = path.resolve(
58	    root,
59	    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-common-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
60	  );
61	  if (commonDir === path.join(root, '.git')) return [];
62	
63	  const gitDir = path.resolve(
64	    root,
65	    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
66	  );
67	  const relativeGitDir = path.relative(commonDir, gitDir); // e.g. worktrees/<name>
68	  return [
69	    '-v',
70	    `${commonDir}:/git-common:ro`,
71	    '-e',
72	    'GIT_COMMON_DIR=/git-common',
73	    '-e',
74	    `GIT_DIR=/git-common/${relativeGitDir}`,
75	    '-e',
76	    'GIT_WORK_TREE=/workspace',
77	  ];
78	}
79	
80	const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
81	const platform = argv[0]?.startsWith('--') ? 'desktop' : (argv[0] ?? 'desktop');
82	if (platform !== 'desktop' && platform !== 'mobile') {
83	  console.error(`[e2e:docker] unknown platform ${JSON.stringify(platform)}. Expected 'desktop' or 'mobile'.`);
84	  process.exit(1);
85	}
86	
87	const group = argv[argv.indexOf('--group') + 1];
88	if (argv.includes('--group')) {
89	  const groups = specGroups();
90	  if (!groups[group]) {
91	    console.error(
92	      `[e2e:docker] unknown group ${JSON.stringify(group)}. Known groups: ${Object.keys(groups).join(', ')}`,
93	    );
94	    process.exit(1);
95	  }
96	}
97	const groupArgs = argv.includes('--group') ? ['--group', group] : [];
98	
99	// A conservative default: unlike a bare-metal CI runner, this shares the
100	// Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on
101	// the host, so CI's `max-instances: 4` (a dedicated runner) is not a safe
102	// default here. Override with `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N` for a VM given more
103	// cores; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has.
104	const maxInstances = process.env.E2E_MAX_INSTANCES ?? '2';
105	
106	const run = (cmd, args) => spawnSync(cmd, args, { cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' }).status ?? 1;
107	
108	if (argv.includes('--build')) {
109	  const build = run('docker', ['compose', '-f', composeFile, 'build']);
110	  if (build !== 0) process.exit(build);
111	}
112	
113	// scripts/run-e2e.mjs itself sets OBSIDIAN_E2E_MOBILE on the wdio subprocess
114	// when `platform` is 'mobile' — no need to also set it at the container level.
115	//
116	// e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh, not a plain `xvfb-run` wrapper — see
117	// that script's own header for why (its signal-based readiness wait hung
118	// indefinitely in this container).
119	const command = ['e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh', platform, ...groupArgs];
120	const status = run('docker', [
121	  'compose',
122	  '-f',
123	  composeFile,
124	  'run',
125	  '--rm',
126	  '-e',
127	  `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=${maxInstances}`,
128	  ...gitVolumeAndEnvArgs(),
129	  'e2e',
130	  ...command,
131	]);
132	process.exit(status);

content.text:
All four pieces are built, wired together, and validated against a real running container/Obsidian instance — not just written and assumed. Summary:

**1. Narrow mode** — [scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs](scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs), `npm run test:e2e:narrow -- <spec> [grep]`. Measured the setup steps (build, hub-gen, drift-snapshot) at under 0.5s combined — they were never the bottleneck, so I kept them rather than adding speculative conditionals; the real win is targeting one spec file directly instead of a whole group. Took an iteration from minutes to ~14s in testing.

**2. Docker + Xvfb** — [e2e/docker/](e2e/docker/), `npm run test:e2e:docker[:mobile] [-- --group <name>]`. Ran the smoke group inside a real Linux/arm64 container end-to-end (`platform: linux` in the reporter output confirms it), with a deliberately-failing scratch test to prove failure detection works there too. Hit and fixed two real bugs along the way, documented in the code/README:
- `xvfb-run`'s signal-based readiness wait hung indefinitely in-container; replaced with a small script that polls for the X socket file instead.
- The worktree's `.git` pointer doesn't resolve inside the container (and this host's OrbStack silently drops same-path bind mounts); fixed via `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` pointed at a differently-mounted git dir.
- A first version shadowed the whole `.obsidian-cache` with a named volume, which hid the failure summary from the host — caught it, rescoped the volume to just the binary subdirectories.

Not built: multi-container parallelism across groups. CI's matrix already covers that; documented why in the README rather than reimplementing it locally.

**3. Docs** — added an "E2E testing" section to [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (symlinked as CLAUDE.md) stating CI is the source of truth for full-suite validation, and [e2e/docker/README.md](e2e/docker/README.md) for the container path specifics.

**4. Structured failure reporting** — added `@wdio/json-reporter` alongside the existing `obsidian` reporter in both wdio configs, with a custom `onComplete` in [e2e/wdio.shared.mts](e2e/wdio.shared.mts) that collapses every worker's dump into `.obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` — verified with a real pass and a real deliberate failure (`jq`-able, one stable path, works identically for narrow/grouped/full and local/container runs).

One thing I didn't run: the `:mobile` variant of the Docker path specifically (only tested `desktop`) — it's the same well-exercised code path with `OBSIDIAN_E2E_MOBILE` already handled by the unmodified `run-e2e.mjs`, so risk is low, but flagging that I didn't execute it.

All changes pass `npm run build`, `lint`, `build:e2e`, and the full unit suite (1077 tests). Nothing under `src/plugin/` or `openspec/` was touched, and `test-vault/` is untouched by any of the runs above.

65	move up, move down) invoked by command id against real notes: text
66	transforms match the spec'd behavior, cursor lands correctly, every accepted
67	operation is a single undo step restoring the exact prior text, and every
68	rejection shows its message while leaving the document byte-identical.

# e2e-verification Specification

## Purpose
Defines the automated end-to-end verification harness: a real (sandboxed) Obsidian
instance driven against a throwaway copy of `test-vault/` to exercise behavior that only
exists in a live app — command dispatch, keyboard grammar, on-disk byte fidelity, and
persistence across restarts — replacing the manual dev-vault checklist it supersedes.
## Requirements
### Requirement: Sandboxed real-Obsidian harness

The project SHALL provide an automated end-to-end harness that launches a
real Obsidian instance with the built plugin installed and a throwaway copy
of `test-vault/`, runnable with a single command (`npm run test:e2e`). The
harness MUST NOT modify the checked-in `test-vault/` and MUST NOT affect the
plugin bundle, the vitest suite, or the plugin typecheck.

#### Scenario: One-command run against a sandbox

- **WHEN** a developer runs `npm run test:e2e`
- **THEN** the plugin is rebuilt, Obsidian launches against a sandboxed copy
  of `test-vault/` with the plugin enabled, all e2e specs run, and after the
  run `git status` shows no changes under `test-vault/`

#### Scenario: Harness excluded from bundle and unit tests

- **WHEN** `npm run build:plugin`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` execute
- **THEN** none of them compile, bundle, or run any file under `e2e/`

### Requirement: Outline mode e2e verification

The harness SHALL verify outline-mode lifecycle end-to-end: toggling by
command id shows a notice and leaves file bytes and mtime unchanged; mode
survives an app restart with no trace in note content; mode follows renames;
deletion prunes the path from plugin data; structural commands are absent on
non-outline notes.

#### Scenario: Toggle leaves file untouched

- **WHEN** the toggle command runs on an open note and the buffer is saved
- **THEN** a notice appears and the note's on-disk bytes and mtime equal
  their pre-toggle values

#### Scenario: Mode persists across restart

- **WHEN** outline mode is enabled for a note and Obsidian is restarted
  preserving state
- **THEN** the note is still in outline mode (grammar keys act) and its
  content contains no mode marker

#### Scenario: Rename follows, delete prunes

- **WHEN** an outline note is renamed, and separately when one is deleted
- **THEN** `data.json` lists the new path after rename and no longer lists
  the deleted path after delete

#### Scenario: Commands gated to outline notes

- **WHEN** command availability is checked on a non-outline note
- **THEN** the four structural commands report unavailable, and on an
  outline note they report available

### Requirement: Structural command e2e verification

The harness SHALL verify the four structural commands (indent, outdent,
move up, move down) invoked by command id against real notes: text
transforms match the spec'd behavior, cursor lands correctly, every accepted
operation is a single undo step restoring the exact prior text, and every
rejection shows its message while leaving the document byte-identical.

#### Scenario: Indent/outdent round-trip with undo

- **WHEN** a paragraph under a paragraph is indented and then outdented
- **THEN** it becomes a `- item` with the cursor after `- `, the outdent
  restores the original text exactly, and one undo keystroke reverses each
  step

#### Scenario: Heading demote keeps links resolving

- **WHEN** a heading section with an incoming `[[note#Heading]]` link is
  demoted
- **THEN** subtree `#` markers shift, body lines are untouched, and the link
  still resolves via the metadata cache

#### Scenario: Skip-level outdent in two steps

- **WHEN** outdent runs twice on `### x` nested under `# y`
- **THEN** the first invocation yields `## x` without moving it and the
  second yields `# x` as a sibling of `# y`

#### Scenario: Moves swap wholesale and renumber

- **WHEN** move up/down runs on a same-level heading section and on an item
  in an ordered list
- **THEN** heading sections swap wholesale and ordered list runs renumber

#### Scenario: Every rejection cue is inert

- **WHEN** each rejection case runs (h6 indent, h1 outdent, top-level
  outdent, indent with nothing above, indent after code fence, outdent of
  section content, cross-kind move)
- **THEN** the matching rejection notice text appears and the buffer is
  byte-identical to before the command

### Requirement: Keyboard grammar e2e verification

The harness SHALL verify the outline keyboard grammar with real key events:
Tab/Shift+Tab indent/outdent at the cursor node, the move-node default
hotkey (Mod+Shift+Up/Down) moves nodes,
Enter splits per node kind, Shift+Enter continues an item as one node, atom
interiors behave stock, keys behave stock when mode is off, and a mode
toggle takes effect on the very next keypress. Each accepted grammar
operation MUST be one undo step; each rejected one MUST change nothing but
show its cue.

#### Scenario: Off-mode keys are stock

- **WHEN** Tab, Enter, and Shift+Enter are pressed in a list in
  a non-outline note
- **THEN** the buffer changes match stock Obsidian behavior (no grammar
  transforms, no notices)

#### Scenario: Toggle applies to the next keypress

- **WHEN** outline mode is toggled while the note is open and a grammar key
  is pressed immediately after
- **THEN** the keypress follows the new mode

#### Scenario: Tab family and moves

- **WHEN** Tab / Shift+Tab / Mod+Shift+Up / Mod+Shift+Down are pressed at a node
- **THEN** the node indents/outdents/moves per the grammar, the cursor lands
  at content start (for indents), and ordered runs renumber

#### Scenario: Enter split semantics per kind

- **WHEN** Enter is pressed mid-item (childless), mid-item (with children), at
  item end, at paragraph end, and on a heading
- **THEN** respectively: the childless item splits into siblings; the parent
  item's remainder becomes its new first child above the existing children; an
  empty `- ` sibling appears with the cursor after the marker; a blank line plus
  cursor appears and typed text becomes the sibling; an empty line appears
  below the heading and typed text becomes a child paragraph

#### Scenario: Shift+Enter keeps one node

- **WHEN** Shift+Enter is pressed inside an item and a structural op then
  targets that item
- **THEN** an aligned continuation line is inserted and the op treats the
  item plus continuation as a single node

#### Scenario: Atom interiors are stock

- **WHEN** Enter, Shift+Enter, and Tab are pressed inside a code fence in an
  outline note
- **THEN** stock editing behavior applies, while the same keys on the
  fence's first line perform whole-fence operations

### Requirement: Shell behavior e2e verification

The harness SHALL verify plugin shell behaviors: disabling the plugin
removes its commands, and the coexistence warning for conflicting plugins
fires once and is not repeated after restart.

#### Scenario: Clean unload

- **WHEN** the plugin is disabled at runtime
- **THEN** its commands are no longer registered

#### Scenario: Coexistence warning fires once

- **WHEN** a conflicting plugin id is enabled and the plugin loads, and
  Obsidian is then restarted
- **THEN** the warning notice appears on the first load and does not appear
  after the restart

### Requirement: Manual protocol reduced to residue

`openspec/changes/editor-core/verification.md` SHALL be rewritten so each
automated checklist item points to the e2e spec covering it, leaving only
genuinely manual checks (mobile smoke, visual polish) as a short manual
residue list.

#### Scenario: Checklist items map to specs

- **WHEN** a reader opens `verification.md` after this change
- **THEN** every previously manual, now-automated item names the e2e spec
  file that covers it, and the remaining manual items are explicitly listed
  as residue

schema: spec-driven

context: |
  Obsidian plugin: a true outliner experience (Logseq/Workflowy/Roam-class).
  Core vision: the "universal isomorphic outline view" — any markdown note maps losslessly
  onto its inherent block tree (headings, paragraphs, lists, other blocks as nodes); a UI
  toggle turns any note into an outline and back; structure is enforced (node-level
  selection/ops, no way to corrupt the tree).
  Architecture (decided): editor-centric — CodeMirror 6 extensions inside the standard
  markdown view via registerEditorExtension, plus own panes for later layers. 100% public
  Obsidian APIs, no private APIs, no monkey-patching; target a clean community-directory
  scorecard (obsidianmd/eslint-plugin from day 1).
  Metadata (decided): native ^block-ids only on demand; collapse state in plugin data;
  markdown files stay clean and fully usable without the plugin.
  v1 (decided): small solid core — editing grammar + node selection + enforced invariants;
  fold persistence, zoom/breadcrumbs, structured backlinks, refs/mirrors are later layers.
  Background research: docs/research/ (landscape, plugin gap analysis, API feasibility,
  open questions/decision log).
githubCopilot:
  cloudAgent: true

# Injected into the matching artifact's generation prompt. Repo-wide conventions live
# in AGENTS.md; these cover only what OpenSpec itself writes.
rules:
  proposal:
    - Include a Non-goals section naming what this change deliberately leaves
      alone.
    - Cite the measurement or research note a claim rests on; never assert a
      figure inline.
  design:
    - Point at the relevant docs/research/ note instead of restating its
      findings.
  specs:
    - Capabilities are flat under specs/; preserve an existing capability's path
      exactly.
  tasks:
    - A task that adds a test also states its negative control - the change that
      must make it fail.
    - The final task is `openspec validate <change> --strict`.

# Advisory guidance returned by `openspec instructions apply|archive --json`.
operations:
  apply:
    guidance:
      - Run the unit suite and the e2e group covering the touched area; the full
        sweep is CI's job.
      - Confirm a new test fails with the fix disabled before trusting that it
        passes with it.
      - Assert relationships in e2e, never absolute glyph widths - CI's fonts
        differ from macOS.
      - Re-measure after widening a predicate; a relaxed condition admits inputs
        nobody considered.
  archive:
    guidance:
      - Archive on the change's own branch, before the PR merges.
      - Bump the version in the same PR, and check the test vault for drift.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(e2e): add narrow mode, containerized runs, and structured failure reports

Three additions to the local e2e dev loop, all aimed at the same problem: a
one-line fix during review required re-running a whole spec group (up to ten
Obsidian launches, ~4 minutes) just to check it and run the negative
control, with no way to see which test failed without scrolling or
re-running narrower.

- scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs (`npm run test:e2e:narrow -- <spec> [grep]`) drives
  wdio directly against one spec file, optionally one test by name, instead
  of a whole group. Measured the build/hub-gen/drift-snapshot setup steps at
  under half a second combined, so they stay in place — the actual cost was
  Obsidian launching once per spec file in a group, and targeting one file
  is what removes it.

- e2e/docker/ (`npm run test:e2e:docker[:mobile]`) runs the suite inside a
  Linux container under Xvfb, so nothing pops up on the host regardless of
  platform. One container per invocation, whatever's in scope (the whole
  suite or one group) — batching is inherited from run-e2e.mjs's own
  dispatch, not reimplemented. Handles two things that don't show up outside
  a container: xvfb-run's signal-based readiness wait hangs indefinitely
  here (replaced with a socket-poll script), and a git worktree's `.git`
  pointer doesn't resolve inside the container (resolved via
  GIT_DIR/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE against a differently-mounted git
  dir, since this host's bind mounts silently no-op when source and target
  paths are identical).

- @wdio/json-reporter alongside the existing `obsidian` reporter, collapsed
  by a new onComplete hook (e2e/wdio.shared.mts) into one small
  `.obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` per invocation — narrow, grouped, full,
  local or containerized — naming every failed test, its spec file, and its
  error message without needing to scroll a group's stdout or re-run
  narrower to find out.
EOF
)"

## Summary

Three additions to the local e2e dev loop, aimed at one problem observed
during a review-fixing session: a one-line fix required re-running a whole
spec group (up to ten Obsidian launches, ~4 minutes) to verify it and its
negative control, with no way to see which test failed without scrolling
raw stdout or re-running narrower.

- **Narrow mode** (`npm run test:e2e:narrow -- <spec> [grep]`) targets one
  spec file, optionally one test by name, instead of a whole group. The
  build/hub-gen/drift-snapshot setup steps stay in place — measured at
  under half a second combined, so skipping them buys nothing. The actual
  cost was Obsidian launching once per spec file in a group; targeting one
  file directly is the entire speedup (minutes → ~10–30s).
- **Containerized runs** (`npm run test:e2e:docker[:mobile]`, `e2e/docker/`)
  run the suite inside a Linux container under Xvfb, so nothing pops up on
  the host regardless of platform. One container per invocation, whatever's
  in scope — batching is inherited from `run-e2e.mjs`'s own dispatch, not
  reimplemented. See `e2e/docker/README.md` for the two container-specific
  issues this hit and fixed (a hung `xvfb-run` readiness wait, and a git
  worktree's `.git` pointer not resolving inside the container).
- **Structured failure reports**: `@wdio/json-reporter` alongside the
  existing `obsidian` reporter, collapsed by a new `onComplete` hook into
  one small `.obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` per invocation — narrow,
  grouped, full, local or containerized — naming every failed test, its
  spec file, and its error message.

`AGENTS.md` gains an "E2E testing" section documenting narrow mode as the
default dev loop, `run-e2e.mjs`'s group/full-suite runs as a pre-checkpoint
check, and CI's per-group matrix as the actual source of truth for a green
full suite. `openspec/config.yaml`'s apply-operation guidance is updated to
match (it previously pointed sessions at a full group run during
iteration).

Infrastructure only — nothing under `src/plugin/` changed, and no
`openspec/changes/` artifacts were touched (this isn't a product-capability
change, so it skips the propose/apply/sync-specs cycle; see the PR
discussion for why `openspec/specs/e2e-verification/spec.md` itself wasn't
touched either).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build:e2e`, `npm test` all pass
- [x] `npm run test:e2e:narrow -- 00-smoke "boots with the plugin loaded"` — real

- [ ] `npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile` specifically (only `desktop` was run
      through the container path; `mobile` shares the same `run-e2e.mjs`

EOF
)"

content.text:
## Spec review

Checked `openspec/specs/*/spec.md` and `openspec/config.yaml` for consistency:

- **`openspec/specs/e2e-verification/spec.md`** — no change needed. Its requirements describe what the harness must guarantee (`npm run test:e2e` rebuilds, sandboxes the vault, leaves `test-vault/` untouched, etc.), and those guarantees still hold exactly as before — narrow mode and the Docker path are additional entry points into the same harness, not a change to its contract. Editing this directly would also bypass this repo's own propose → apply → sync-specs process for versioned capabilities, which the original infra request explicitly said to stay out of.
- **`openspec/config.yaml`** — did need an update. Its `operations.apply.guidance` (injected into every `openspec-apply-change` run) told sessions to "run the unit suite and the e2e group covering the touched area" while iterating — now the slower of the two options. Updated it to point at narrow mode instead, with a pointer to AGENTS.md.

content.text:
Docs alone don't hold — anyone (agent or human) who already knows the old `npm run test:e2e -- --group X` incantation, or types the raw `wdio --spec ... --mochaOpts.grep ...` from muscle memory, just bypasses AGENTS.md entirely since nothing reads it back to them at the moment of the mistake. The lever that actually generalizes is making the *expensive path warn about itself when taken*, not just documenting the cheap one:

- **Runtime nudge in `run-e2e.mjs`** (cheapest, catches everyone): when it's about to launch more than ~2-3 spec files outside `CI=true`, print a one-line reminder pointing at `test:e2e:narrow` before proceeding. No blocking, fires exactly when the costly choice is made, works for a human in a terminal exactly as well as an agent.
- **A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook** (agent-specific, more targeted): pattern-match the raw `wdio run ... --spec ... --mochaOpts.grep` incantation or `npm run test:e2e -- --group` in Bash calls and inject a reminder before it runs. Catches the exact bypass this session rediscovered, but only helps Claude Code sessions, adds a hook to maintain, and needs care not to nag on the legitimate "final check before a checkpoint" case.

I'd start with the first one since it's low-cost and helps regardless of who's driving — want me to add it, and/or the hook?

#!/bin/sh
# Starts a virtual X server and runs the e2e suite against it.
#
# Not `xvfb-run`: its SIGUSR1-based readiness wait hung indefinitely in this
# container — Xvfb came up (confirmed via `ps`/`docker exec`), but the
# wrapped command never launched, because the `wait` in xvfb-run's own
# script never returned. Polling for the X server's own socket file is a
# more reliable readiness check in a container than that signal handshake —
# verified by running the suite end to end with this script.
#
# `@wdio/local-runner` (used by wdio-obsidian-service) would otherwise try
# to manage its own Xvfb per worker via `@wdio/xvfb`, which shells out to
# `xvfb-run` under the hood — the same mechanism that hung. Exporting
# DISPLAY here makes it skip that entirely: `XvfbManager.shouldRun()` treats
# an already-set DISPLAY as "not a headless environment" and does nothing.
set -e

Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1280x1024x24 -nolisten tcp &
XVFB_PID=$!
trap 'kill $XVFB_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT

tries=50
while [ ! -e /tmp/.X11-unix/X99 ]; do
  tries=$((tries - 1))
  if [ $tries -le 0 ]; then
    echo "[start-xvfb-and-run] Xvfb did not come up in time" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

export DISPLAY=:99
exec node scripts/run-e2e.mjs "$@"

    xvfb \
    xauth \

    libnss3 \

# Dependencies are baked into the image at build time (Linux binaries for
# esbuild, Electron, etc). The compose file mounts a volume over

# has Linux binaries on a macOS/Windows host — see e2e/docker/README.md.

#!/bin/sh
# Starts a virtual X server, exports DISPLAY, and execs the given command
# against it — e.g. `node scripts/run-e2e.mjs desktop` or
# `node scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs <spec>`.
#
# Not `xvfb-run`: its readiness handshake (wait for a SIGUSR1 from Xvfb) can
# hang indefinitely in a container, with Xvfb up but the wrapped command
# never launched. Polling for the X server's own socket file is a more
# reliable readiness check here. Exporting DISPLAY before the command also
# makes @wdio/xvfb's own auto-management (used by @wdio/local-runner) a
# no-op — it only acts when DISPLAY is unset.
set -e

Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1280x1024x24 -nolisten tcp &
XVFB_PID=$!
trap 'kill $XVFB_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT

tries=50
while [ ! -e /tmp/.X11-unix/X99 ]; do
  tries=$((tries - 1))
  if [ $tries -le 0 ]; then
    echo "[start-xvfb-and-run] Xvfb did not come up in time" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

export DISPLAY=:99
exec "$@"

#!/bin/sh
# Starts a virtual X server and runs the e2e suite against it.
#
# Not `xvfb-run`: its SIGUSR1-based readiness wait hung indefinitely in this
# container — Xvfb came up (confirmed via `ps`/`docker exec`), but the
# wrapped command never launched, because the `wait` in xvfb-run's own
# script never returned. Polling for the X server's own socket file is a
# more reliable readiness check in a container than that signal handshake —
# verified by running the suite end to end with this script.
#
# `@wdio/local-runner` (used by wdio-obsidian-service) would otherwise try
# to manage its own Xvfb per worker via `@wdio/xvfb`, which shells out to
# `xvfb-run` under the hood — the same mechanism that hung. Exporting
# DISPLAY here makes it skip that entirely: `XvfbManager.shouldRun()` treats
# an already-set DISPLAY as "not a headless environment" and does nothing.
set -e

Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1280x1024x24 -nolisten tcp &
XVFB_PID=$!
trap 'kill $XVFB_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT

tries=50
while [ ! -e /tmp/.X11-unix/X99 ]; do
  tries=$((tries - 1))
  if [ $tries -le 0 ]; then
    echo "[start-xvfb-and-run] Xvfb did not come up in time" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

export DISPLAY=:99
exec node scripts/run-e2e.mjs "$@"

1	/**
2	 * Runs the e2e suite inside a Linux container under Xvfb — see
3	 * `e2e/docker/README.md` for what this buys over running locally (nothing
4	 * pops up on the host, whatever OS the host is) and its limits.
5	 *
6	 *   node scripts/e2e-docker.mjs [desktop|mobile] [--group <name>]
7	 *   node scripts/e2e-docker.mjs [desktop|mobile] <spec> [test-name-grep]
8	 *
9	 * One container per invocation, however many spec files that covers — every
10	 * spec (the default), one CI-style group with `--group`, or one spec (and
11	 * optionally one test) via `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` when a bare positional
12	 * argument follows the platform. Not one container per spec file:
13	 * `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`/`scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` inside the container
14	 * already dispatch every spec in scope through a single wdio invocation, so
15	 * batching is inherited, not reimplemented here.
16	 *
17	 * This deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run groups in
18	 * parallel, the way CI's matrix does: CI already gives full-suite,
19	 * parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section —
20	 * it's the source of truth for that), so this script's job is narrower:
21	 * let a local run happen without a window, not out-race the matrix.
22	 */
23	
24	import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
25	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
26	import * as os from 'node:os';
27	import * as path from 'node:path';
28	import { specGroups } from './spec-groups.mjs';
29	
30	const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
31	const composeFile = path.join(root, 'e2e', 'docker', 'docker-compose.yml');
32	
33	/**
34	 * A git WORKTREE's `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
35	 * (`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree
36	 * alone gives the container that pointer with nothing at the far end, so
37	 * every git-invoking step (the build stamp in esbuild.config.mjs, and
38	 * `git status`/`checkout` in scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs) fails with "not
39	 * a git repository".
40	 *
41	 * Bind-mounting the real git dir at the SAME absolute path — the more
42	 * obvious fix — does not work on every host (confirmed failing on OrbStack:
43	 * a bind mount whose source and target path are identical silently mounts
44	 * nothing). So instead the git dir is mounted at an arbitrary container path
45	 * and `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` point git at it directly,
46	 * bypassing `.git`-file resolution entirely.
47	 *
48	 * The common dir is mounted read-only — it's the shared object store, no
49	 * reason a container run should write there — but the worktree's OWN gitdir
50	 * under it is mounted again, read-write, nested on top: `git checkout`
51	 * during vault-drift cleanup needs to create `index.lock` inside that
52	 * worktree-specific directory, which a blanket read-only mount would block.
53	 *
54	 * A plain (non-worktree) checkout's `--git-common-dir` is just `.git` under
55	 * the already-mounted root, so this is a no-op there.
56	 */
57	function gitVolumeAndEnvArgs() {
58	  const commonDir = path.resolve(
59	    root,
60	    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-common-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
61	  );
62	  if (commonDir === path.join(root, '.git')) return [];
63	
64	  const gitDir = path.resolve(
65	    root,
66	    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
67	  );
68	  // POSIX separators regardless of host OS: this becomes part of a Linux
69	  // container path (GIT_DIR), and path.relative on Windows returns
70	  // backslashes.
71	  const relativeGitDir = path.relative(commonDir, gitDir).split(path.sep).join('/');
72	  return [
73	    '-v',
74	    `${commonDir}:/git-common:ro`,
75	    '-v',
76	    `${gitDir}:/git-common/${relativeGitDir}:rw`,
77	    '-e',
78	    'GIT_COMMON_DIR=/git-common',
79	    '-e',
80	    `GIT_DIR=/git-common/${relativeGitDir}`,
81	    '-e',
82	    'GIT_WORK_TREE=/workspace',
83	  ];
84	}
85	
86	/**
87	 * Runs the container as the invoking user instead of the image's default
88	 * root, so files it writes into the bind-mounted repo (build output, the
89	 * generated backlink fixture, e2e-summary.json) and into the Obsidian
90	 * download volumes stay owned by that user — not root — on the host. On a
91	 * native Linux host (unlike Docker Desktop/OrbStack's VM) root-owned output
92	 * from a bind mount is a real, sticky problem: it breaks the next host-side
93	 * build and can make git refuse the checkout as an "unsafe repository"
94	 * owned by someone else.
95	 *
96	 * `os.userInfo().uid/gid` are `-1` on Windows (no POSIX UID/GID there), so
97	 * this is a no-op on that platform — Docker Desktop for Windows containers
98	 * don't have the same host-ownership concern.
99	 */
100	function userArgs() {
101	  const { uid, gid } = os.userInfo();
102	  if (uid < 0 || gid < 0) return [];
103	  // HOME=/tmp: this UID has no /etc/passwd entry in the image, and npm/node
104	  // otherwise warn or fail trying to resolve a home directory for it.
105	  return ['-u', `${uid}:${gid}`, '-e', 'HOME=/tmp'];
106	}
107	
108	const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
109	const platform = argv[0] === 'mobile' ? 'mobile' : 'desktop';
110	const rest = argv[0] === 'desktop' || argv[0] === 'mobile' ? argv.slice(1) : argv;
111	
112	const groupIndex = rest.indexOf('--group');
113	const group = groupIndex === -1 ? undefined : rest[groupIndex + 1];
114	if (group !== undefined) {
115	  const groups = specGroups();
116	  if (!groups[group]) {
117	    console.error(
118	      `[e2e:docker] unknown group ${JSON.stringify(group)}. Known groups: ${Object.keys(groups).join(', ')}`,
119	    );
120	    process.exit(1);
121	  }
122	}
123	// A bare positional (not --group's own value) selects narrow mode — one
124	// spec, optionally one test — mirroring scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs's own CLI.
125	const positional = rest.filter((a, i) => {
126	  if (a.startsWith('--')) return false;
127	  if (groupIndex !== -1 && i === groupIndex + 1) return false; // --group's own value
128	  return true;
129	});
130	const [narrowSpec, narrowGrep] = group === undefined ? positional : [];
131	
132	// A conservative default: unlike a bare-metal CI runner, this shares the
133	// Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on
134	// the host, so CI's `max-instances: 4` (a dedicated runner) is not a safe
135	// default here. Override with `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N` for a VM given more
136	// cores; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has.
137	const maxInstances = process.env.E2E_MAX_INSTANCES ?? '2';
138	
139	const run = (cmd, args) => spawnSync(cmd, args, { cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' }).status ?? 1;
140	
141	const innerCommand = narrowSpec
142	  ? ['node', 'scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs', narrowSpec, ...(narrowGrep ? [narrowGrep] : []), ...(platform === 'mobile' ? ['--mobile'] : [])]
143	  : ['node', 'scripts/run-e2e.mjs', platform, ...(group !== undefined ? ['--group', group] : [])];
144	
145	const status = run('docker', [
146	  'compose',
147	  '-f',
148	  composeFile,
149	  'run',
150	  // Not optional: `docker compose run` reuses whatever image already exists
151	  // and does NOT check the Dockerfile or package.json for changes on its
152	  // own — confirmed by editing the Dockerfile and running without --build,
153	  // which used the stale image silently. With --build every run pays only
154	  // Docker's own per-layer cache cost (sub-second when nothing changed).
155	  '--build',
156	  '--rm',
157	  '-e',
158	  `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=${maxInstances}`,
159	  ...userArgs(),
160	  ...gitVolumeAndEnvArgs(),
161	  'e2e',
162	  'e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh',
163	  ...innerCommand,
164	]);
165	process.exit(status);

content.content:
1	# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)
2	
3	`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
4	macOS/Windows. CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb instead
5	(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ubuntu-latest`) — this reproduces that locally in a container, so a
6	run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host, whatever OS it runs.
7	
8	## Invoke
9	
10	```bash
11	npm run test:e2e:docker                    # whole suite, desktop
12	npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke   # one CI-style group
13	npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile             # mobile-emulation config
14	```
15	
16	Both wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose` (`docker-compose.yml` in this
17	directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also validates `--group` against
18	`scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir handling described below.
19	
20	The image builds automatically on first run (and on any later `Dockerfile`/`package.json`
21	change, via Docker's own layer cache) — pass `--build` to force a rebuild.
22	
23	## What's actually verified, not assumed
24	
25	Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
26	app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
27	it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
28	uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
29	one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.
30	
31	## Design choices
32	
33	**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
34	default, or one group with `--group`. Never one container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`
35	inside the container already dispatches every spec in scope through a single wdio run,
36	parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers, so batching multiple files per container
37	invocation is inherited from the existing script rather than reimplemented here. This
38	deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
39	matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
40	testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.
41	
42	`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
43	CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
44	Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
45	`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
46	give.
47	
48	**No `xvfb-run`.** `e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh` starts `Xvfb` itself and polls for its
49	socket file before exporting `DISPLAY` and launching the suite — see that script's header. The
50	obvious choice, wrapping the whole invocation in `xvfb-run --auto-servernum`, hung indefinitely in
51	this container: `Xvfb` came up but the wrapped `node` process never started, because the
52	`wait`/`SIGUSR1` handshake `xvfb-run`'s own shell script uses for readiness never completed.
53	
54	**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
55	`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime,
56	`docker-compose.yml` mounts a *named volume* over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the
57	bind-mounted repo's `node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules`
58	(wrong-platform native binaries) would sit in front of the image's. Docker seeds a fresh named
59	volume from what's already visible at that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra
60	setup step.
61	
62	Three more named volumes persist what `obsidian-launcher` downloads (Obsidian itself, its
63	installer, and the Electron/Chromedriver build — ~490MB together, measured) across container
64	runs — scoped to exactly those subdirectories under `.obsidian-cache`, deliberately NOT the whole
65	directory: `e2e-summary.json` and `e2e-reports/` (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section) land
66	under `.obsidian-cache` too, on every run, and need to stay on the bind-mounted host filesystem —
67	`cat .obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` right after the container exits is the whole point of that
68	file. An earlier version of this compose file shadowed the whole directory with one volume, which
69	worked but made the summary invisible outside the container; this is why it doesn't.
70	
71	**Rebuild the image or drop a volume** after a dependency or Obsidian-version change that isn't
72	reflected some other way: `docker volume ls` to see the actual names (`docker compose` prefixes
73	them, e.g. `docker_e2e-node-modules`), `docker volume rm <name>` to drop one.
74	
75	## Worktree caveat
76	
77	A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
78	(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
79	that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
80	`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
81	a git repository".
82	
83	`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
84	arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
85	bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
86	more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and
87	target path are identical, confirmed with a plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before
88	reaching for the env-var approach instead.) A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this —
89	`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already `.git` under the mounted root.
90

# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)

`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
macOS/Windows. CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb instead
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ubuntu-latest`) — this reproduces that locally in a container, so a
run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host, whatever OS it runs.

## Invoke

```bash
npm run test:e2e:docker                    # whole suite, desktop
npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke   # one CI-style group
npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile             # mobile-emulation config
```

Both wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose` (`docker-compose.yml` in this
directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also validates `--group` against
`scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir handling described below.

The image builds automatically on first run (and on any later `Dockerfile`/`package.json`
change, via Docker's own layer cache) — pass `--build` to force a rebuild.

## What's actually verified, not assumed

Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Design choices

**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
default, or one group with `--group`. Never one container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`
inside the container already dispatches every spec in scope through a single wdio run,
parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers, so batching multiple files per container
invocation is inherited from the existing script rather than reimplemented here. This
deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.

`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
give.

**No `xvfb-run`.** `e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh` starts `Xvfb` itself and polls for its
socket file before exporting `DISPLAY` and launching the suite — see that script's header. The
obvious choice, wrapping the whole invocation in `xvfb-run --auto-servernum`, hung indefinitely in
this container: `Xvfb` came up but the wrapped `node` process never started, because the
`wait`/`SIGUSR1` handshake `xvfb-run`'s own shell script uses for readiness never completed.

**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime,
`docker-compose.yml` mounts a *named volume* over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the
bind-mounted repo's `node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules`
(wrong-platform native binaries) would sit in front of the image's. Docker seeds a fresh named
volume from what's already visible at that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra
setup step.

Three more named volumes persist what `obsidian-launcher` downloads (Obsidian itself, its
installer, and the Electron/Chromedriver build — ~490MB together, measured) across container
runs — scoped to exactly those subdirectories under `.obsidian-cache`, deliberately NOT the whole
directory: `e2e-summary.json` and `e2e-reports/` (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section) land
under `.obsidian-cache` too, on every run, and need to stay on the bind-mounted host filesystem —
`cat .obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` right after the container exits is the whole point of that
file. An earlier version of this compose file shadowed the whole directory with one volume, which
worked but made the summary invisible outside the container; this is why it doesn't.

**Rebuild the image or drop a volume** after a dependency or Obsidian-version change that isn't
reflected some other way: `docker volume ls` to see the actual names (`docker compose` prefixes
them, e.g. `docker_e2e-node-modules`), `docker volume rm <name>` to drop one.

## Worktree caveat

A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
a git repository".

`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and
target path are identical, confirmed with a plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before
reaching for the env-var approach instead.) A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this —
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already `.git` under the mounted root.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)

`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
macOS/Windows. CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb instead
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ubuntu-latest`) — this reproduces that locally in a container, so a
run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host, whatever OS it runs.

## Invoke

```bash
npm run test:e2e:docker                    # whole suite, desktop
npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke   # one CI-style group
npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile             # mobile-emulation config
```

Both wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose` (`docker-compose.yml` in this
directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also validates `--group` against
`scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir handling described below.

The image builds automatically on first run (and on any later `Dockerfile`/`package.json`
change, via Docker's own layer cache) — pass `--build` to force a rebuild.

## What's actually verified, not assumed

Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Design choices

**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
default, or one group with `--group`. Never one container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`
inside the container already dispatches every spec in scope through a single wdio run,
parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers, so batching multiple files per container
invocation is inherited from the existing script rather than reimplemented here. This
deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.

`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
give.

**No `xvfb-run`.** `e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh` starts `Xvfb` itself and polls for its
socket file before exporting `DISPLAY` and launching the suite — see that script's header. The
obvious choice, wrapping the whole invocation in `xvfb-run --auto-servernum`, hung indefinitely in
this container: `Xvfb` came up but the wrapped `node` process never started, because the
`wait`/`SIGUSR1` handshake `xvfb-run`'s own shell script uses for readiness never completed.

**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime,
`docker-compose.yml` mounts a *named volume* over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the
bind-mounted repo's `node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules`
(wrong-platform native binaries) would sit in front of the image's. Docker seeds a fresh named
volume from what's already visible at that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra
setup step.

Three more named volumes persist what `obsidian-launcher` downloads (Obsidian itself, its
installer, and the Electron/Chromedriver build — ~490MB together, measured) across container
runs — scoped to exactly those subdirectories under `.obsidian-cache`, deliberately NOT the whole
directory: `e2e-summary.json` and `e2e-reports/` (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section) land
under `.obsidian-cache` too, on every run, and need to stay on the bind-mounted host filesystem —
`cat .obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` right after the container exits is the whole point of that
file. An earlier version of this compose file shadowed the whole directory with one volume, which
worked but made the summary invisible outside the container; this is why it doesn't.

**Rebuild the image or drop a volume** after a dependency or Obsidian-version change that isn't
reflected some other way: `docker volume ls` to see the actual names (`docker compose` prefixes
them, e.g. `docker_e2e-node-modules`), `docker volume rm <name>` to drop one.

## Worktree caveat

A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
a git repository".

`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and
target path are identical, confirmed with a plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before
reaching for the env-var approach instead.) A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this —
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already `.git` under the mounted root.

#!/bin/sh
# Starts a virtual X server, exports DISPLAY, and execs the given command
# against it — e.g. `node scripts/run-e2e.mjs desktop` or
# `node scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs <spec>`.
#
# Not `xvfb-run`: its readiness handshake (wait for a SIGUSR1 from Xvfb) can
# hang indefinitely in a container, with Xvfb up but the wrapped command
# never launched. Polling for the X server's own socket file is a more
# reliable readiness check here. Exporting DISPLAY before the command also
# makes @wdio/xvfb's own auto-management (used by @wdio/local-runner) a
# no-op — it only acts when DISPLAY is unset.
set -e

Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1280x1024x24 -nolisten tcp &
XVFB_PID=$!
trap 'kill $XVFB_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT

tries=50
while [ ! -e /tmp/.X11-unix/X99 ]; do
  tries=$((tries - 1))
  if [ $tries -le 0 ]; then
    echo "[start-xvfb-and-run] Xvfb did not come up in time" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

export DISPLAY=:99
exec "$@"

7	 *   node scripts/e2e-docker.mjs [desktop|mobile] <spec> [test-name-grep]

10	 * spec (the default), one CI-style group with `--group`, or one spec (and
11	 * optionally one test) via `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` when a bare positional
12	 * argument follows the platform. Not one container per spec file:
13	 * `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`/`scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` inside the container
14	 * already dispatch every spec in scope through a single wdio invocation, so
15	 * batching is inherited, not reimplemented here.
16	 *
17	 * This deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run groups in
18	 * parallel, the way CI's matrix does: CI already gives full-suite,
19	 * parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section —
20	 * it's the source of truth for that), so this script's job is narrower:
21	 * let a local run happen without a window, not out-race the matrix.
22	 */
23	
24	import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
25	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
26	import * as os from 'node:os';
27	import * as path from 'node:path';
28	import { specGroups } from './spec-groups.mjs';
29	
30	const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
31	const composeFile = path.join(root, 'e2e', 'docker', 'docker-compose.yml');
32	
33	/**
34	 * A git WORKTREE's `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
35	 * (`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree
36	 * alone gives the container that pointer with nothing at the far end, so
37	 * every git-invoking step (the build stamp in esbuild.config.mjs, and
38	 * `git status`/`checkout` in scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs) fails with "not
39	 * a git repository".
40	 *
41	 * Bind-mounting the real git dir at the SAME absolute path — the more
42	 * obvious fix — is not reliable: some Docker file-sharing backends no-op a
43	 * bind mount whose source and target path are identical, mounting nothing.
44	 * So instead the git dir is mounted at an arbitrary container path and
45	 * `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` point git at it directly,
46	 * bypassing `.git`-file resolution entirely.
47	 *
48	 * The common dir is mounted read-only — it's the shared object store, no
49	 * reason a container run should write there — but the worktree's OWN gitdir
50	 * under it is mounted again, read-write, nested on top: `git checkout`
51	 * during vault-drift cleanup needs to create `index.lock` inside that
52	 * worktree-specific directory, which a blanket read-only mount would block.
53	 *
54	 * A plain (non-worktree) checkout's `--git-common-dir` is just `.git` under
55	 * the already-mounted root, so this is a no-op there.
56	 */
57	function gitVolumeAndEnvArgs() {
58	  const commonDir = path.resolve(
59	    root,
60	    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-common-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
61	  );
62	  if (commonDir === path.join(root, '.git')) return [];
63	
64	  const gitDir = path.resolve(
65	    root,
66	    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
67	  );
68	  // POSIX separators regardless of host OS: this becomes part of a Linux
69	  // container path (GIT_DIR), and path.relative on Windows returns
70	  // backslashes.
71	  const relativeGitDir = path.relative(commonDir, gitDir).split(path.sep).join('/');
72	  return [
73	    '-v',
74	    `${commonDir}:/git-common:ro`,
75	    '-v',
76	    `${gitDir}:/git-common/${relativeGitDir}:rw`,
77	    '-e',
78	    'GIT_COMMON_DIR=/git-common',
79	    '-e',
80	    `GIT_DIR=/git-common/${relativeGitDir}`,
81	    '-e',
82	    'GIT_WORK_TREE=/workspace',
83	  ];
84	}
85	
86	/**
87	 * Runs the container as the invoking user instead of the image's default
88	 * root, so files it writes into the bind-mounted repo (build output, the
89	 * generated backlink fixture, e2e-summary.json) and into the Obsidian
90	 * download volumes stay owned by that user — not root — on the host. On a
91	 * native Linux host (unlike Docker Desktop/OrbStack's VM) root-owned output
92	 * from a bind mount is a real, sticky problem: it breaks the next host-side
93	 * build and can make git refuse the checkout as an "unsafe repository"
94	 * owned by someone else.
95	 *
96	 * `os.userInfo().uid/gid` are `-1` on Windows (no POSIX UID/GID there), so
97	 * this is a no-op on that platform — Docker Desktop for Windows containers
98	 * don't have the same host-ownership concern.
99	 */
100	function userArgs() {
101	  const { uid, gid } = os.userInfo();
102	  if (uid < 0 || gid < 0) return [];
103	  // HOME=/tmp: this UID has no /etc/passwd entry in the image, and npm/node
104	  // otherwise warn or fail trying to resolve a home directory for it.
105	  return ['-u', `${uid}:${gid}`, '-e', 'HOME=/tmp'];
106	}
107	
108	const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
109	const platform = argv[0] === 'mobile' ? 'mobile' : 'desktop';
110	const rest = argv[0] === 'desktop' || argv[0] === 'mobile' ? argv.slice(1) : argv;
111	
112	const groupIndex = rest.indexOf('--group');
113	const group = groupIndex === -1 ? undefined : rest[groupIndex + 1];
114	if (group !== undefined) {
115	  const groups = specGroups();
116	  if (!groups[group]) {
117	    console.error(
118	      `[e2e:docker] unknown group ${JSON.stringify(group)}. Known groups: ${Object.keys(groups).join(', ')}`,
119	    );
120	    process.exit(1);
121	  }
122	}
123	// A bare positional (not --group's own value) selects narrow mode — one
124	// spec, optionally one test — mirroring scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs's own CLI.
125	const positional = rest.filter((a, i) => {
126	  if (a.startsWith('--')) return false;
127	  if (groupIndex !== -1 && i === groupIndex + 1) return false; // --group's own value
128	  return true;
129	});

131

133	// Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on
134	// the host, so CI's `max-instances: 4` (a dedicated runner) is not a safe

153	  '-f',
154	  composeFile,
